questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the CREATE ... CLONE command in Snowflake?

options.text: To create zero-copy clones of databases, schemas, and tables
To physically duplicate all micro-partitions immediately
To create a read-only replica in another region
To export data to external cloud storage

explanation.correct: CREATE ... CLONE is primarily used to create zero-copy clones of databases, schemas, and tables (and other schema objects), sharing the same underlying storage as the source until data diverges.

distractors.B: Cloning does not immediately duplicate storage; clones share the source's micro-partitions until changes occur.
distractors.C: Cross-region read-only replicas are created by replication, not cloning.
distractors.D: Exporting to external storage is done with COPY INTO <location>, not cloning.

questions.stem: What is true about the relationship between a clone and its source after cloning?

options.text: Changes to the source automatically propagate to the clone
The clone is read-only and cannot be modified
The clone is writable and independent; changes are not reflected in the other object
The clone and source must always share the same schema forever

explanation.correct: A clone is writable and independent of its source. Changes made to the source or the clone are not reflected in the other object.

distractors.A: Source changes do not propagate to the clone; they are independent.
distractors.D: The clone is independent and its schema can diverge from the source.

questions.stem: By default, do CREATE <object> ... CLONE statements copy privilege grants from the source object to the clone?

options.text: Yes, all grants including OWNERSHIP are always copied
Grants are copied only for databases, never for tables
Grants are never copyable under any circumstances
No; most objects do not copy grants unless COPY GRANTS is specified (where supported)

explanation.correct: For most objects, CREATE ... CLONE does not copy grants. Commands that support COPY GRANTS (e.g., CREATE TABLE, CREATE VIEW) can optionally copy all privileges except OWNERSHIP.

distractors.A: OWNERSHIP is never copied via COPY GRANTS, and grants aren't copied by default.
distractors.B: Tables can copy grants via COPY GRANTS; the statement is incorrect.
distractors.C: Grants can be copied using the COPY GRANTS clause where supported.

questions.stem: When you clone a database or schema, which THREE statements about the child objects are correct? (Select THREE)

options.text: The clone inherits all granted privileges on the clones of child objects
Cloning a database recursively clones all its schemas and objects
The clone of the container itself inherits privileges granted on the source container
Cloning a schema recursively clones all contained objects
External tables are cloned with full data copied
Only the top-level container is cloned, not its contents

explanation.correct: The clone inherits privileges on child object clones, and cloning is recursive: cloning a database clones its schemas/objects, and cloning a schema clones its contained objects.

distractors.C: The clone of the container itself does NOT inherit privileges granted on the source container.
distractors.E: External tables are not cloned when using Time Travel; and cloning shares storage rather than copying data.
distractors.F: Cloning includes contents recursively, not just the top-level container.

questions.stem: Which TWO access-control privileges are required on the SOURCE object to clone it? (Select TWO)

options.text: MODIFY on a source table
OWNERSHIP on a source database
SELECT on a source table
USAGE on a source database
CREATE TABLE on the source table

explanation.correct: To clone a table you need SELECT on the source table; to clone a database you need USAGE on the source database.

distractors.A: MODIFY is not the privilege required to clone a table; SELECT is.
distractors.B: OWNERSHIP on a database is not required to clone it; USAGE is.
distractors.E: CREATE TABLE is needed on the target container, not as a source-table privilege for cloning.

questions.scenario: A developer clones a single table that references a sequence defined in a different schema.
questions.stem: A developer clones objects that reference a sequence. Which TWO statements about which sequence the cloned table references are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: If you clone just the table, the cloned table references the source sequence
If the sequence is in a different database/schema, the cloned table references the source sequence
Cloning just the table always creates a new copy of the sequence
The column's default sequence is dropped during cloning
A random system-generated sequence replaces the original

explanation.correct: If you clone just the table, or the sequence is in a different database/schema, the cloned table references the SOURCE sequence. It references a cloned sequence only when the shared container is cloned.

distractors.C: Cloning just the table does not create a new sequence copy; it references the source sequence.
distractors.D: The default sequence is retained, not dropped.
distractors.E: No random system sequence replaces the original.

questions.scenario: A team clones a table that has a clustering key and relies on Automatic Clustering.
questions.stem: What is the default state of automatic clustering on the newly cloned table?

options.text: Automatic Clustering is suspended by default on the new table
Automatic Clustering runs immediately at full cost
The clustering key is dropped from the clone
The clone cannot have a clustering key

explanation.correct: A cloned table is created with a clustering key, but by default Automatic Clustering is suspended. You resume it with ALTER TABLE <name> RESUME RECLUSTER.

distractors.B: Automatic Clustering does not run immediately; it is suspended by default.
distractors.C: The clustering key is retained on the clone.
distractors.D: The clone can and does have a clustering key.

questions.scenario: An engineer clones a database that contains internal named stages and wants those internal stages included in the clone.
questions.stem: Which clause must be specified?

options.text: COPY GRANTS
WITH MANAGED ACCESS
INCLUDE INTERNAL STAGES
IGNORE HYBRID TABLES

explanation.correct: Internal named stages are cloned only if you use the INCLUDE INTERNAL STAGES clause when cloning a database or schema.

distractors.A: COPY GRANTS copies privileges, not internal stages.
distractors.B: WITH MANAGED ACCESS controls managed access schemas, not internal stage cloning.
distractors.D: IGNORE HYBRID TABLES skips hybrid tables; it does not include internal stages.

questions.scenario: A data engineer clones a database and reviews how stages are handled in the clone.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about cloning stages are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Data files in table stages are copied to the clone
Cloning an external stage copies the referenced cloud storage bucket contents
External named stages present at the start of the operation are cloned
Cloned table stages are empty (data files in the source are not copied)
Internal named stages are always cloned by default

explanation.correct: When cloning a database/schema, external named stages present at the start are cloned, and cloned table stages are empty because data files in source table stages are not copied.

distractors.A: Data files in table stages are NOT copied to the clone.
distractors.B: Cloning an external stage has no impact on the referenced cloud storage contents.
distractors.E: Internal named stages are cloned only when INCLUDE INTERNAL STAGES is specified, not by default.

questions.scenario: A DBA clones a schema and wants the cloned tables to copy privileges from the source tables (excluding ownership).
questions.stem: Which clause enables copying these grants?

options.text: INCLUDE INTERNAL STAGES
COPY GRANTS
WITH MANAGED ACCESS
IGNORE TABLES WITH INSUFFICIENT DATA RETENTION

explanation.correct: COPY GRANTS (supported by commands like CREATE TABLE ... CLONE) copies all privileges except OWNERSHIP from the source to the new object.

distractors.A: INCLUDE INTERNAL STAGES clones internal stages, not privileges.
distractors.C: WITH MANAGED ACCESS relates to managed access schemas, not grant copying.
distractors.D: IGNORE TABLES WITH INSUFFICIENT DATA RETENTION skips purged tables during Time Travel clones.

questions.scenario: A developer needs to clone objects at a past point using the AT | BEFORE clause and is checking which object types support it.
questions.stem: For which object types does CREATE ... CLONE support the AT | BEFORE (Time Travel) clause?

options.text: Databases, schemas, and non-temporary tables
Only external tables
Only internal stages
Only users and roles

explanation.correct: For databases, schemas, and non-temporary tables, CLONE supports the AT | BEFORE clause for cloning using Time Travel.

distractors.B: External tables are not cloned when using Time Travel.
distractors.C: Internal stages are not cloned via the Time Travel clause.
distractors.D: Users and roles are not schema objects cloned with AT | BEFORE.

questions.scenario: A developer clones a database using AT(TIMESTAMP => ...) and wants to skip child tables whose historical data has already been purged from Time Travel.
questions.stem: Which TWO clauses are relevant to controlling this Time Travel clone behavior? (Select TWO)

options.text: COPY GRANTS
IGNORE TABLES WITH INSUFFICIENT DATA RETENTION
WITH MANAGED ACCESS
IGNORE HYBRID TABLES
ENABLE FAILOVER

explanation.correct: For databases/schemas, CLONE supports IGNORE TABLES WITH INSUFFICIENT DATA RETENTION (skip tables purged from Time Travel) and IGNORE HYBRID TABLES (skip hybrid tables).

distractors.A: COPY GRANTS copies privileges; it does not control Time Travel skipping.
distractors.C: WITH MANAGED ACCESS relates to managed access schemas.
distractors.E: ENABLE FAILOVER is a replication/connection setting, unrelated to cloning.

questions.stem: Which THREE parameters can the AT | BEFORE clause accept when cloning with Time Travel? (Select THREE)

options.text: VERSION
SNAPSHOT_ID
TIMESTAMP
OFFSET (time difference in seconds)
ALIAS
STATEMENT (query ID)

explanation.correct: The AT | BEFORE clause accepts TIMESTAMP, OFFSET (seconds from present), or STATEMENT (a query ID).

distractors.A: VERSION is not an AT | BEFORE parameter.
distractors.B: SNAPSHOT_ID is not a Snowflake Time Travel parameter.
distractors.E: ALIAS applies to model versions, not Time Travel cloning.

questions.scenario: A table has a foreign key constraint referencing a primary-key table in the SAME schema, and the whole schema is cloned.
questions.stem: What does the cloned table with the foreign key reference?

options.text: The primary key in the other cloned table (within the clone)
The primary key in the source table
Nothing; the foreign key is dropped
A newly generated surrogate key

explanation.correct: When the database or schema containing both tables is cloned, the cloned table with the foreign key references the primary key in the other cloned table.

distractors.B: It references the source primary key only when the tables are in separate databases/schemas that aren't cloned together.
distractors.C: The foreign key is retained, not dropped.

questions.scenario: A developer runs CREATE TABLE ... CLONE and later modifies the source table's data.
questions.stem: How does this affect the clone's storage and data?

options.text: The clone's data changes to match the source
The clone is invalidated and must be recreated
Both source and clone are locked until a refresh
The clone remains unchanged; new micro-partitions are created only for changed data

explanation.correct: Clones share underlying storage with the source at creation. When either side changes, Snowflake creates new micro-partitions only for the changed data; the clone remains independent and unchanged by source edits.

distractors.A: The clone is independent; source data changes do not alter the clone.
distractors.B: The clone is not invalidated by source changes.
distractors.C: Cloning does not lock the source and clone; they operate independently.

questions.scenario: A DBA is reviewing which schema objects can be cloned with CREATE ... CLONE beyond databases, schemas, and tables.
questions.stem: Which THREE additional objects can be cloned with CREATE ... CLONE? (Select THREE)

options.text: Users
Network policies
External stages
File formats
Resource monitors
Sequences

explanation.correct: Beyond databases/schemas/tables, CREATE ... CLONE can clone other schema objects including external stages, file formats, sequences, streams, tasks, alerts, and database roles.

distractors.A: Users are account-level objects, not cloned via CREATE ... CLONE.
distractors.B: Network policies are not schema objects cloned by CREATE ... CLONE.
distractors.E: Resource monitors are account-level objects, not cloned via CREATE ... CLONE.

questions.scenario: An engineer clones a database that contains a pipe object.
questions.stem: Which role has the OWNERSHIP privilege on the cloned pipes?

options.text: The role that owned the source pipes
The role that creates the clone
The ACCOUNTADMIN role only
No role; pipes cannot be cloned

explanation.correct: For pipes, the role that creates the clone has the OWNERSHIP privilege on the pipes.

distractors.A: Ownership is assigned to the cloning role, not the source pipe's owner.
distractors.C: It is the cloning role, not necessarily ACCOUNTADMIN.
distractors.D: Pipes are cloned when their containing database/schema is cloned.

questions.scenario: A team clones an Apache Iceberg table and inspects the metadata of the clone versus the source.
questions.stem: What is true about the cloned Iceberg table's metadata?

options.text: The clone shares the exact same metadata.json and table-uuid as the source
The clone has no metadata until first queried
The clone has its own metadata.json with a unique table-uuid
Metadata is stored only in the source's cloud bucket

explanation.correct: For cloned Iceberg tables, Snowflake generates distinct metadata files: the clone has its own metadata.json with a unique table-uuid, last-sequence-number, and other properties.

distractors.A: The clone does NOT share the same metadata.json or table-uuid.
distractors.B: The clone has its own metadata generated at clone time, not on first query.
distractors.D: The clone's metadata is distinct and not merely in the source bucket.

questions.scenario: A developer uses CREATE SCHEMA ... CLONE with a Time Travel timestamp and notices some objects were not cloned into the timestamped schema.
questions.stem: Which TWO object types are NOT cloned in the described Time Travel scenarios? (Select TWO)

options.text: Regular (non-temporary) tables
External tables
Views
User tasks when using CREATE SCHEMA ... TIMESTAMP
Sequences

explanation.correct: External tables are not cloned when using Time Travel, and user tasks in a schema are not cloned when using CREATE SCHEMA ... at a TIMESTAMP (they are cloned when no timestamp is used).

distractors.C: Views are cloned as part of the schema.
distractors.E: Sequences are cloned; the cloned table references the cloned sequence when the container is cloned.

questions.scenario: For an Iceberg table using Snowflake-managed storage, a developer tries CREATE ICEBERG TABLE ... CLONE where the source is transient and the new table is permanent.
questions.stem: What is the result?

options.text: The clone succeeds and converts the type automatically
The statement fails; the source and new table must both be transient or both permanent
The clone succeeds but becomes read-only
The clone succeeds only with COPY GRANTS

explanation.correct: For Iceberg tables using Snowflake-managed storage, CREATE ICEBERG TABLE ... CLONE succeeds only when the source and new table are both transient or both permanent; a transient/permanent mismatch fails.

distractors.A: There is no automatic type conversion; the mismatch causes failure.
distractors.C: The clone does not succeed as read-only; it fails.
distractors.D: COPY GRANTS does not resolve the transient/permanent mismatch.
